August 11, 2026

Cigna Appeals Department  
[Appeals mailing address or electronic submission location provided by Cigna]

Re: Expedited reconsideration/appeal of denial of total ankle replacement  
Member: Sawyer Alvarez  
Member ID: W635441117  
Plan: Cigna Commercial/ACA, Ohio  
Requested service: Total ankle replacement  
CPT: 27702  
Reference number: POC-A1F3D3C000-86797  
Date of denial notice: August 11, 2026

Dear Cigna Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal Cigna’s denial of prior authorization for total ankle replacement, CPT 27702. The denial states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan’s criteria for medical necessity. I respectfully request that Cigna reverse the denial and authorize the procedure based on the clinical evidence submitted with the prior authorization request.

The records establish medically significant, progressive ankle disease and failure of appropriate nonoperative treatment:

- I have had 12 months of progressive ankle pain that has not improved with rest.
- I completed 18 supervised physical therapy visits over 10 weeks, from April 18, 2026, through June 27, 2026. The therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance, and the physical therapy discharge note documents completion.
- I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 29, 2026, provided only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- Weight-bearing ankle radiographs obtained June 2, 2026, show obliteration of the tibiotalar joint space with subchondral cysts, findings consistent with advanced structural ankle joint disease.
- My function is substantially impaired: I walk with an antalgic gait and can ambulate only approximately two blocks.
- Examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- The treating orthopedic surgeon, Duval, MD, has evaluated the condition and requested total ankle replacement.
- The record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

These findings demonstrate persistent symptoms, objective radiographic disease, functional limitation, and failure of prolonged conservative care. They also support the medical necessity of definitive surgical treatment rather than continued ineffective nonoperative management. The request is for treatment of a documented, symptomatic, structurally advanced ankle condition, not for elective treatment based only on pain without objective findings.

The denial does not identify which specific medical-necessity requirement was allegedly not satisfied. Please conduct a full reconsideration using the records listed above and the complete prior authorization packet. If Cigna maintains the denial, please identify the exact criterion that was found unmet, explain how the submitted records fail to satisfy it, and provide the clinical rationale and records relied upon in making that determination.

I also request a copy of the exact medical policy version and all clinical-review criteria, plan-specific guidelines, or other medical-necessity criteria applied to this request. I have not quoted the plan’s policy in this appeal because the policy text was not provided to me in the denial notice. Please evaluate this appeal under the policy and criteria actually applicable to my request and its August 11, 2026 denial date.

Please reverse the adverse benefit determination and approve total ankle replacement, CPT 27702. If Cigna requires additional information, please contact Duval, MD, directly through the provider information in the authorization packet or contact me at [member telephone number] or [member mailing address]. This appeal is submitted within the 180-day appeal period stated in the denial notice, which ends February 7, 2027.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Alvarez  
[Member mailing address]  
[Member telephone number]  
[Member email address, if applicable]
